Sockystick 1.0.7

Sockystick 1.0.7 resolves hostnames on your LAN DNS server before proxying, so split-horizon names (for example a Pi-hole local record) reach your LAN services instead of their public WAN addresses.

  • LAN DNS Resolution: The local bridge looks up each hostname on your LAN DNS server (auto-detected from the system's private IPv4 resolver, e.g. Pi-hole) and forwards the LAN address to the remote SOCKS5 proxy. TLS SNI and Host headers are unchanged, so the right virtual host and certificate are still selected. Lookups that fail, time out, or are blocked fall back to remote resolution. Configurable in Settings → General → LAN DNS, with an optional server override and domain list.
  • Fail-Fast Upstream Errors: When the remote SOCKS5 server is unreachable or refuses the connection, the bridge now returns an immediate “connection refused” reply instead of leaving browser connections hanging.
  • Bridge Without Authentication: The local bridge now also runs for unauthenticated proxies when LAN DNS resolution is enabled.
  • Test Isolation: Running the test suite no longer clears the app's saved proxy settings.

Sockystick 1.0.6

Sockystick 1.0.6 adds clean connection handoff for Safari and iCloud Private Relay so Safari immediately obeys the SOCKS5 proxy on connect and returns cleanly on disconnect.

  • Safari & iCloud Private Relay Handoff: Automatically restarts Safari's background Safari Networking XPC process on connect, disconnect, and quit (keeping windows and tabs open) so cached iCloud Private Relay QUIC tunnels and stale proxy pools are flushed immediately. Configurable in Settings → General.
  • Clean Bridge Teardown: Tracks and closes all active bridged connections when stopping the local SOCKS5 auth bridge, and disables the macOS SOCKS5 proxy before stopping the bridge to eliminate transition errors.
  • Default Host: Defaults the proxy host to 127.0.0.1 instead of a private LAN address for fresh setups.

Sockystick 1.0.5

Sockystick 1.0.5 aligns the application icon with Apple's macOS Human Interface Guidelines icon grid and Dock proportions.

  • Dock Icon Alignment: Adjusted the icon layout to Apple's standard 824×824 pt squircle grid with standard optical padding and drop shadow, ensuring it renders at the exact same size as all other macOS apps in the Dock.
